title: Expose the scoped session credential digest to Foundation dispatch
description:
Production prerequisite filed by task-aedeb1745c7b473ea92c1f1da723bc4b for task-fc9660b0a4f24891908a11e303a7c347 unblock clause (3). Measurement at HEAD 9adceb7 names the durable source of bootstrapCredentialDigest as SessionRecord.credentialSha256: agent-wrapper.ts mints the per-agent secret, session.open persists SHA-256(secret), and the same secret is delivered to the spawned child as its scoped MCP bearer. The provider-profile aggregate is the wrong identity (project/profile, not project/session), provider API environment tokens are a separate credential axis, and activation/attempt records only relay the value after launch.

Implement a focused production reader, proposed symbol readSessionCredentialDigest(store, projectId, sessionId), over readSessionLedger. It must return the exact stored credentialSha256 only for the named project/session when the ledger is readable and the session is OPEN. It must fail closed without exposing the digest: store/codec/corrupt-ledger failure preserves SESSION_LEDGER_UNREADABLE at DAEMON_PREREQUISITE; absent, foreign-project, or CLOSED session returns a stable SESSION_CREDENTIAL_DIGEST_UNAVAILABLE at DAEMON_PREREQUISITE (or an architect-approved equally stable closed vocabulary, chosen once and pinned). Contain store throws. Do not hash provider API tokens, MOE_DAEMON_CREDENTIAL, profile data, or caller payload. Do not add the digest to ProviderRuntimeObservation or ProviderProfileRevision.

Consumer edge: task-fc9660b0 will call this reader using server-derived identities (authenticated principal project/session and the durable activation lease ownerSessionRef), pass code/layer untranslated, and replace the caller-carried launchTemplate.bootstrapCredentialDigest. This row owns the reader surface/tests only; fc9660b0 owns handler composition and caller-field retirement.
definitionOfDone: A production readSessionCredentialDigest-equivalent reads SessionRecord.credentialSha256 through readSessionLedger, project- and session-scoped, returns it only for an OPEN session, and contains store throws.

Failure outcomes are fail-closed and stable: corrupt/unreadable/store failure asserts SESSION_LEDGER_UNREADABLE + DAEMON_PREREQUISITE; absent, foreign-project, and CLOSED assert SESSION_CREDENTIAL_DIGEST_UNAVAILABLE + DAEMON_PREREQUISITE (or one architect-approved replacement vocabulary pinned consistently). No refusal includes plaintext or digest.

Tests drive the production reader for success, absent, foreign project, CLOSED, malformed stored hash, unreadable ledger, and throwing store; every refusal asserts exact reason code and layer and asserts no digest field.
A mutation drill deleting the project/session/status binding makes the named foreign-project/CLOSED assertion red; a zero-case sweep is forbidden.
The consumer is explicitly task-fc9660b0a4f24891908a11e303a7c347; its follow-up composition must use this reader rather than a duplicate helper.
taskRails: Named source is SessionRecord.credentialSha256 with preimage agent-wrapper's per-agent secret; provider profile, provider API credentials, operator bootstrap credentials, and caller payload are forbidden substitutes.
Preserve the existing session ledger's project filter, malformed-record fail-closed behavior, and stable reason-code/layer attribution.

TWO STRENGTHENINGS BEYOND THE PLAN, both defensive against a green-but-vacuous arm:
(a) ARM 5 CARRIES ITS OWN POSITIVE CONTROL. Before the malformed seed, the SAME raw fact set is committed unmodified through `commitRaw` and asserted to read back ok with the right digest. Without it, arm 5 could be red because my hand-built fact object was the wrong shape for `parseOpened` for some unrelated reason — and it would then stay red (i.e. keep "passing") even if the hash check were deleted. The control makes exactly ONE field the difference. The fact set is copied from `openSession`'s committed `facts` literal (capabilities, credentialSha256, expiresAt, keyEpochRef, principalId, recoveryIncarnationRef, sessionId), using the fixture's TEST_RECOVERY_* refs so the recovery-ref checks pass.
(b) THE ANTI-LEAK ASSERTION SWEEPS THE SERIALISED REFUSAL, not a named field: `Object.hasOwn(result, "credentialSha256")` is false AND `/[0-9a-f]{64}/u` does not match `JSON.stringify(result)`. A digest smuggled into `detail`, or into a field nobody thought to name, still reddens. It is invoked per-arm inside `expectRefusal`, so a leak added to ONE arm reds that arm's own test rather than a single global check.

NOT DONE, deliberately: no reader-side re-check of the hash shape (step 1 proved `parseOpened` already re-checks it on read, so such a guard is unreachable dead code and its "test" would be answered by an earlier layer). State is never hand-folded — every arm seeds through `runSessionCommand` or through `commitRaw`'s production-ingress-decoded seam.

RESTORE INSTRUMENT — SHA-256, NOT `git diff`. The two main deliverables are UNTRACKED on first landing, and `git diff -- <untracked path>` returns EMPTY whether the file is pristine, mutated, or deleted — it would have "proven" a restore that never happened. Baseline digest of session-credential-digest.ts = e79fa92f8c7d89aa07929114dc40a0be3aec8ea6d416df269accd01265a71f1e; every drill printed the post-restore digest and every one read MATCH. The runner also refuses to proceed if the mutation left the digest unchanged (a mutation that applied nothing reads exactly like a green drill), restores inside `finally` so a crash cannot leave a mutant on disk, and asserts each anchor occurs EXACTLY ONCE before substituting. Runner lives at %TEMP%\drill-worker-934d8b66.py — never in the repo (epic rail 5) and never in MSYS /tmp.

PER-DRILL RED, each naming the arm it killed (a drill that reds the WRONG arm proves nothing):
1. STATUS BINDING deleted (`record === undefined || record.status !== "OPEN"` -> `record === undefined`) -> 1 failed / 6 passed. Killed: "refuses a CLOSED session, so a revoked credential cannot be re-read". The CLOSED arm is answered by THIS guard, not by an earlier layer.
2. SESSION BINDING deleted (`sessions.get(sessionId)` -> first ledger entry) -> 1 failed. Killed: "refuses an absent session id without revealing whether it ever existed". DISCLOSURE: the success arm survived this one, because the fixture holds a single session so "first entry" IS the right entry — the plan anticipated it ("may"). Drill 7 below closes that gap properly rather than leaving the success arm unmutated.
3. PROJECT BINDING deleted (`readSessionLedger(store, projectId)` -> hardcoded "project-session-1") -> 1 failed. Killed: "refuses a foreign project with the SAME code as an absent session". This is the anti-oracle guard; it is live.
4. DIGEST LEAK (UNAVAILABLE refusal rebuilt to carry `record?.credentialSha256 ?? ""`) -> 3 failed / 4 passed. Killed all three UNAVAILABLE arms: CLOSED, foreign-project, absent. The CLOSED arm leaks a REAL stored digest here, not a fabricated constant, so this proves the anti-leak clause catches an actual disclosure and is not decorative. It reds on THREE arms, which is the per-arm grading the plan asked for.
5. THROW CONTAINMENT removed (`try {...} catch {` -> `if (store !== null) {...} else {`) -> 1 failed. Killed: "contains a throwing store instead of propagating the throw to its caller".
6. ADDED BY ME — UNREADABLE BRANCH deleted (the whole `if (ledger.unreadable)` block removed) -> 2 failed / 5 passed. Killed: the malformed-stored-hash arm AND the unreadable-ledger arm. WHY IT MATTERS: without it, the reader's own fail-closed branch had no mutant. Deleting it does not crash — control falls through to `sessions.get`, finds nothing, and answers SESSION_CREDENTIAL_DIGEST_UNAVAILABLE. That is precisely the fail-open the fold exists to prevent (corrupt bytes reading as a free session id), and it would have been invisible to a green suite and to the plan's five drills.
7. ADDED BY ME — DIGEST IDENTITY (`credentialSha256: record.credentialSha256` -> `"0".repeat(64)`) -> 2 failed / 5 passed. Killed: the success arm AND arm 5's positive control. This is the mutant drill 2 could not produce, and it is what makes the success arm's BYTE-equality assertion load-bearing: a reader returning some other well-formed 64-hex value dies here. Every one of the 7 test arms is now killed by at least one drill.

ADVERSARIAL SELF-REVIEW, run before completing — one real fix, three findings disclosed:
- FIXED: `let ledger;` was an evolving-any. Now `let ledger: SessionLedger;` with a type-only import. Typecheck re-run EXIT 0 and the suite re-run 7/7 after the change.
- Hostile INPUTS all fail closed, checked by reading not guessing: empty-string sessionId or projectId -> UNAVAILABLE; oversized/injection-shaped ids are only ever Map keys and JS string compares, never SQL; `"__proto__"` is safe specifically because `ledger.sessions` is a real Map — had the fold used a plain object, that lookup would have been a prototype hit and a genuine bug.
- CONCURRENCY: pure read, no check-then-act, no shared mutable state, no handles opened, nothing to clean up on the error path. The fold pages the store, so a write landing between pages can produce a torn read — that is pre-existing fold behaviour I inherit and do not worsen. Consequence for the consumer, and I have written it into the fc9660b0 comment: a successful read is NOT a lease, since the session can close immediately after. If dispatch needs OPEN-ness at effect time it must check on the write path.
- Coverage of the try/catch is narrow ON PURPOSE: only the `readSessionLedger` call is wrapped. `Map.get` and `Object.freeze` cannot throw here, and widening the catch would let a future bug inside the reader be silently reported as an unreadable ledger.
